page.layout: One printed page of text in a single column, with running head at top right and page number at top left. Below the text, a division heading "CAPUT" stands at the right, with no notes in the margins.

main_text.p: Nec abit Becanus à sententia Protestantium in affirmando, hasce duas propositiones, qui-bus totus Papismus nititur, 1. Petrum fuis-se vicarium Christi, tum caput, Pastorem & rectorem totius Ecclesiæ. 2. Papam in ea potestate & in eo munere successisse Petro, nullibi in Sacra Scriptura extare: quanquam dispa-ri consilio, hi ut reficiant tanquam figmentum humanum quicquid in Scriptura non re-peritur: ille ut traditionem suam ꝛquet [?] authoritate Sacræ Scripturæ, in qua tamen traditione, nequidem illæ duæ propositiones in-veniuntur.
main_text.head: CAPUT

page.notes: The word after "suam" is printed as a small symbol followed by "quet"; I read it as "ꝛquet" with uncertainty. The heading CAPUT has no number printed beside it. The faint scattered marks in the lower half of the page are show-through and are not transcribed. The "Digitized by Google" line is the digitiser's banner and is omitted.
